standard.title: Co-construct fair play rules
standard.description: co-construct and apply rules to promote fair play in a range of physical activities
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have followed rules to promote fair play in a range of physical activities (AC9HPFM04). They have practised turn-taking and basic inclusion in game contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students co-construct and apply rules to promote fair play in a range of physical activities.

nodes.label: Purpose of rules in fair play
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how rules contribute to fair play and apply them in group activities.
nodes.minimum_width: In a physical activity, apply a rule and explain why that rule makes the activity fairer.
nodes.typical_width: Across a range of physical activities, apply rules and explain how specific rules contribute to fair play; identify what would change if a rule were removed.
wider: Compare rules across two different activities and identify which rules serve the same fair-play purpose in different forms
Investigate examples of unfair play and identify which rule was absent or broken, and how adding or restoring the rule would help
Discuss rules from a First Nations Australian game and compare the fair-play principles they embody with rules from familiar games
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding why rules exist — not just what they are — is the prerequisite for co-constructing new rules (Node 2). Students who can only follow rules without understanding their purpose cannot meaningfully participate in rule construction.

response_modes.reason: Ask students to explain the 'why' behind a rule, not just state it. A prompt like 'This rule is fair because...' makes the reasoning explicit and surfaces whether students understand the principle or just recall the procedure.

success_criteria: Applies at least one rule correctly in a group physical activity
Explains why that rule makes the activity fairer

nodes.label: Co-constructing and modifying rules
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can participate in co-constructing or modifying rules that make a physical activity fairer or more inclusive.
nodes.minimum_width: With others, suggest or agree to at least one change to a game rule that makes the activity fairer; apply the changed rule.
nodes.typical_width: Participate in discussions to co-construct or modify rules for a range of physical activities; explain how proposed changes improve fairness or inclusion for all learners.
wider: Design a set of rules for a new game from scratch that ensures all players have equitable opportunities to participate
Discuss how a rule change might affect different players differently (e.g. players with different abilities or skill levels) and refine the rule to address this
Compare self-constructed rules with official game rules and identify similarities and differences in the fairness principles each reflects

response_modes.reason: Co-construction of rules is richer when students have encountered it across multiple activity types. Vary the activity context (chasing games, target games, partner activities) so students practise the co-construction process in different movement settings.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Rule co-construction across different activity structures requires students to think about different kinds of fairness — turn-taking, spatial equity, skill balance. Students who have co-constructed rules for diverse activity types develop a more nuanced understanding of what fairness requires than those who have only modified one type of game.
success_criteria: Contributes at least one suggestion during a group rule-making discussion
Applies a co-constructed or modified rule in a physical activity

nodes.label: Turn-taking, sharing and inclusive participation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can demonstrate turn-taking and sharing of equipment when participating in play and minor games, and connect these behaviours to fair play.
nodes.minimum_width: In a group activity, demonstrate turn-taking or equipment sharing and explain how this contributes to fair play.
nodes.typical_width: Consistently demonstrate turn-taking and equipment sharing across a range of minor games and play contexts; link specific behaviours to the fair-play rules in place.
wider: Identify a situation where turn-taking or sharing broke down and propose a rule change or behaviour strategy that would prevent it
Reflect on how including everyone affects the quality of the game for all participants
Observe a game (live or recorded) and identify examples of fair and unfair sharing or turn-taking, linking them to the rules in place

response_modes.reason: Turn-taking and sharing are the behavioural application of the fair-play principles established in Nodes 1 and 2. Use activities that require students to manage both rule application and social behaviour simultaneously — not just practise each in isolation.

success_criteria: Demonstrates turn-taking or equipment sharing in a group physical activity
Explains how this behaviour supports fair play in the activity
